world.eraEvidence: stated years in the narration: 1692 witch trials, 1970s servant flashback, present-day Julia
world.setting: Pemberton, a seventeenth-century estate in rural Massachusetts, and the 1692 village around it
world.register: gothic thriller, dual timeline, present-day plain modern dress against period dress and candlelit rooms

julia.name: Julia
julia.role: present-day protagonist, a woman who loses her job and apartment and moves into the family estate to check on her grandmother
julia.look: a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression

caroline.name: Caroline
caroline.role: 1692 ancestor, a young wife of Archie Eldridge, accused of witchcraft and burned at the stake
caroline.look: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes

peton.name: Peton
peton.role: the estate itself, named in the narration as the house Julia is walking; the family house the book centres on
peton.look: a seventeenth-century timber house, not a person; no figure is drawn for it

ethel.name: Ethel
ethel.role: Julia's great-aunt, elderly, aggressive about protecting the yard
ethel.look: an elderly woman in her eighties, thin, grey hair in a bun, dark cardigan, stern face

henry.name: Henry
henry.role: ambitious curator from the Wood Haven Museum
henry.look: a man in his forties, neat build, short hair, tweed jacket, polite but intense

molly.name: Molly
molly.role: 1692 servant in the Eldridge household, later revealed as a manipulator behind the accusations
molly.look: a young woman in her twenties, plain build, brown hair under a cap, rough servant's dress

celia.name: Celia
celia.role: a 1970s servant at the estate who later appears in the present-day plot, proud and remorseless
celia.look: a woman in her seventies, composed, grey-streaked hair, cardigan, cold expression

eldridge.name: Archie Eldridge
eldridge.role: wealthy, powerful husband, about fifteen years older than Caroline
eldridge.look: a man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face

forest.look: a dark wooded estate edge at night, where a serial killer is said to hunt

bedroom.look: a low old bedroom with a window onto the grounds and a hidden trapdoor in the floor

cafe.look: a small retro diner in town

manuscript.look: the heavy chestnut front door and the old household records of the house

street.look: the iron-fronted street side of the house

objects.why: the book's central theme: who owns a house and what it holds
the family's willingness to bury things on its own property
the estate passing down with its secrets
the bones found in the yard
the iron bear door knocker as protector, and the house as a barrier
the 1692 trials and the present-day legal trap
the estate inherited as a gift that is also a trap
the people hiding behind other identities

spine.claim: Julia moves into Pemberton with nothing left, and the house starts to show its own secrets.
The bones in the yard and Ethel's threats show that the family has been burying its history on its own land.
The 1692 story and the present story are the same story: a house that protects its owners by hiding its dead.
Inheritance turns out to be a debt the family keeps paying in silence.
The house does not belong to the family; the family belongs to the house.
